# ADR-0073: A launch-form choice reads its options from a recorded task output

> **Status:** proposed | **Date:** 2026-11-09

**References:** [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-PARAMS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-params), [ADR-0027](../adr/ADR-0027.md), [ADR-0037](../adr/ADR-0037.md), [ADR-0070](../adr/ADR-0070.md)

## Context

A parameter's choices are written in the params block ([RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-PARAMS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-params)), which must be a literal the engine reads without evaluating the source. The launch form renders the stored schema ([ADR-0027](../adr/ADR-0027.md)), which rejected a controller-side copy of the form definition so the pack stays its single source.

Some choices are data rather than authorship. The backport playbook's target release and component must name a column and a row of the release component spreadsheet, which only a credentialed task can read, and only releases the operator has configured can run. Written into the params block, the list goes stale on every release and costs a draft save and re-pin each time. Left free text, the launcher guesses a spelling and learns at the resolve task, minutes and dollars later, that the release does not exist.

[ADR-0070](../adr/ADR-0070.md) solved the same shape for routes: a choice names a dependency's field, the engine resolves it with bounds, and the record keeps what was offered.

## Decision

A declared parameter MAY carry choices_from = {"task": "<name>", "field": "<field>"} in place of choices. The block stays a literal, so introspection without evaluation still holds.

- **Producer.** The task must be declared in the same workflow and emit the field as a list of strings. The compiler checks the reference against the producer's emits, as keyed does. The producer and its dependency closure must not read params, so they compile and run without any launch values.
- **Snapshot.** The controller keeps, per playbook (registered version or draft head), the field's value from the most recent run in which the producer passed: the choice snapshot, with its run key, capture time, and digest. Any run that includes the producer refreshes it.
- **Refresh.** A choices refresh is a launch that compiles only the producer closure. It needs no parameters, so it can run as a standing launch ([ADR-0037](../adr/ADR-0037.md)) on a schedule or on demand from the playbook page.
- **Bounds.** At most 256 entries of at most 256 characters each. Duplicates collapse to the first. A snapshot outside the bounds is not stored, and the previous one stays.
- **Form and validation.** The schema emits x-choices-from. The form renders the snapshot as a select and shows its age. Launch validation refuses a value outside the snapshot. With no snapshot yet, the field is free text with a notice, and the pack's own checks decide.
- **Record.** A launch records the snapshot's run key and digest beside its params, so a reader sees what was offered without re-running the producer.
- **Dependent values.** choices_from MAY add keyed_by = "<param>", naming another declared parameter. The field is then an object from that parameter's values to option lists, and the form offers the list for the value currently entered, empty until one is. A parameter MAY instead declare placeholder_from = {"task", "field", "keyed_by"}, whose field maps the keyed parameter's values to one string. The form shows that string greyed out in the empty input, as the value the pack will choose itself; it is never submitted. Both read the same snapshot and are bounded the same way.
- **Open choices.** A declaration with choices or choices_from MAY set allow_other = True. The form then adds an "Other" entry that takes free text, and validation accepts any value of the declared type and pattern instead of refusing one outside the list. The list stays a suggestion the author vouches for; the escape hatch is for values the list does not know yet, such as a release added after the last refresh.
- **Other surfaces.** The CLI and ask validation have no snapshot. They validate the declared type only, so the producer's checks remain the authority.

## Consequences

- Data-shaped choices stay current without editing the pack, and a wrong value is refused at the form instead of at the first task.
- Choices are as fresh as the last refresh. A release added to the sheet appears after the next refresh, not the instant it is typed.
- The controller stores one small list per declaring parameter per playbook and serves it with the schema. It does not contact external services or execute pack code when the form opens.
- A producer that reads params is a compile error, so a value that depends on another launch value is precomputed for every key: the producer emits an object keyed by the other parameter's values, and the form selects from it. For the backport pack, release_options emits components per release for target_component and the selected branch per release for target_branch's placeholder.
- With allow_other, a value outside the list reaches the pack, so the pack's own checks must decide it; without it, the form and launch validation refuse it first.
- A placeholder is display only. The pack still makes the choice itself at run time, so a stale placeholder misleads the reader but cannot change the run.
- Packs pinned before this change see no difference. A reader that predates x-choices-from renders the field as plain text.

## Alternatives Considered

### choices_from names a producer task in the same workflow; the controller keeps its latest passing output as the choice snapshot (accepted)

- **Pros:** The params block stays the single, literal source of the form, as [ADR-0027](../adr/ADR-0027.md) requires., The controller neither contacts external services nor executes pack code when a form opens., The same resolve-bound-record shape as [ADR-0070](../adr/ADR-0070.md)'s dynamic route choices.
- **Cons:** Choices are as fresh as the last refresh.

### A pack script regenerates the literal choices list and saves a new draft or version (rejected)

- **Pros:** No engine or controller change.
- **Cons:** Every release costs a draft save, and for a registered pack a re-pin and re-approval., The list in source is stale between regenerations, with nothing showing its age.
- **Rejected because:** It turns data churn into source churn on the path that is meant to change only on review.

### The controller fetches choices itself when the form opens, from a URL or connector the param names (rejected)

- **Pros:** Always current.
- **Cons:** The controller would hold the source's credentials and reach external services on page load., A second definition of the form's data outside the pack, which [ADR-0027](../adr/ADR-0027.md) rejected.
- **Rejected because:** It moves credentials and pack-specific logic into the controller.

### choices_from names another playbook's task output (rejected)

- **Pros:** A small dedicated refresh playbook keeps the main graph untouched.
- **Cons:** Couples two playbooks' versions and permissions; a producer and its consumer can drift apart.
- **Rejected because:** The producer-closure refresh gives the same small run without a cross-playbook reference.
